item.title: Labour Party buys Birżebbuġa club after court ordered it to vacate
item.description: The Labour Party has purchased its Birżebbuġa Labour Club, party president Alex Sciberras announced, more than a year after a Constitutional Court ruling found the party's earlier takeover of the property had breached the owner's fundamental rights and ordered it to vacate.
item.content:encoded:

Sources: Malta Independent, Malta Today

item.title: €60 million reverse osmosis plant planned for Ħal Far
item.description: The Water Services Corporation is to invest around €60 million in a new reverse osmosis plant in Ħal Far, which will increase capacity to produce 40 million litres of potable water a day. The project was unveiled by Energy and Environment Minister Miriam Dalli.

item.title: 'You're a liar': animal rights activists clash in court over cat cafe
item.description: Carmen Coleiro, who managed the cat cafe at the St Vincent de Paul long-term care facility from 2016, was accused of lying by animal rights activist Romina Frendo during the compilation of evidence on Monday. The court heard allegations of starving cats, filthy conditions and misuse of funds at the cafe, which was shut down in 2023, with the activist claiming animals continued to be admitted despite reports of deaths.

item.title: Tourist eco-contribution increase is least welcome Budget measure, survey finds
item.description: In the second release of the Esprimi Budget Barometer 2027, the expansion of Mater Dei Hospital's emergency department and the continuation of energy subsidies were the most welcomed measures, named by 41% and 42% of respondents respectively. The higher eco-contribution on tourist accommodation was named as least welcome by 33% and welcomed by only 8%.

item.title: Two men arrested in Paceville over alleged drug trafficking
item.description: Two men, a 25-year-old Somali national residing in Marsa and a 32-year-old Eritrean residing in Pietà, were arrested late on Saturday during police patrols in Paceville and are to be charged in court with alleged drug trafficking. One of the pair was said to have ditched suspected cocaine when he spotted the officers.

item.title: One dead and two in critical state after boat hits reef off Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq
item.description: A man has died and a second man and a 14-year-old boy are in a critical condition after the boat they were travelling in struck a reef off Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq on Sunday evening. Police were alerted at around 7.15pm that a boat had run aground on the reef known as Is-Sikka s-Safra, with passers-by reporting flares lit on board. The three victims, two men and a boy, were transferred by a Civil Protection Department vessel, treated on the beach by medics and then taken to Mater Dei Hospital, where their condition was described as serious. The Civil Protection Department said the rescue was carried out in close coordination with the Armed Forces of Malta, the police and Mater Dei Hospital emergency staff, and asked the public to avoid the hospital except in genuine emergencies.

item.title: Man, 59, arrested over €4,000 theft from Mrieħel warehouse
item.description: A 59-year-old resident of San Ġwann was arrested after allegedly stealing around €4,000 from a warehouse in Triq l-Intornjatur, Mrieħel, on Saturday night. Police were called out at around 9.30pm to a suspected burglary and found a broken window overlooking the warehouse car park, which officers believe the suspect used to gain entry. The man was found inside an office during the search of the building and the money was recovered. Separately, Times of Malta reported that a 59-year-old man was later arrested in the case.

item.title: Pantomime poster outside Parliament vandalised
item.description: The poster for the Bella u l-Bestja pantomime was found vandalised outside Parliament in Valletta early on Sunday morning, the show's author Rodney Gauci said. Gauci claimed the damage was deliberate rather than wind or accident, and said the poster had been cut from the frame advertising the pantomime, which opens at the end of the year. He called the attack "an attack on the art", and a report was filed with the police, who appealed for information.

item.title: €500 maintenance grant for solar water heaters opens
item.description: Applications opened on Monday for a €500 maintenance grant for households that installed a solar water heater under the 2021 government grant scheme at least five years ago. The Regulator for Energy and Water Services said the scheme is aimed at covering servicing costs for systems bought under the 2021 Solar Water Heater Grant.

Sources: Times of Malta, Lovin Malta

item.title: Mosta residents oppose eight-storey care home recommended for approval
item.description: Residents in Mosta are fighting a proposed 25-metre-high elderly care home in Triq il-Farinal, in the Sgħajtar area, which would replace an existing house with 156 bedrooms accommodating around 362 elderly residents. A Planning Authority hearing on the application is scheduled for Friday.

item.title: Artists hit back at culture minister after claims they think they are 'God's gift to the world'
item.description: Malta's creative community has hit out at Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea after he said many artists believe they are "God's gift to the world" and that art should exist within certain "norms". Speaking at the Festival of Ideas, Agius Galea said that artistic expression has to operate within societal norms, and described his first months in office as "presumptuous and dangerous" and "traumatic" while adapting to a profession where creativity is central. Several prominent figures in the sector publicly questioned his understanding of the sector he oversees, calling him unqualified and out of touch with the people who work in it.

item.title: Żurrieq residents raise €10,000 to fight Nigret development
item.description: Residents of Żurrieq are appealing for donations to raise €10,000 covering the cost of five appeals against development applications in Nigret, warning it is a final chance to stop hundreds of apartments on agricultural land. Two of the five applications have already been approved by the Planning Authority.

item.title: Police recruitment age could rise from 39 to 50, Bedingfield says
item.description: Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said the government is considering raising the maximum age for police recruits from 39 to 50, which would allow older and more experienced candidates to join. Recruits joining above the current limit would not qualify for the full 25-year pension arrangement but would receive a pro-rata pension. Around 80 new recruits have started training and are expected to graduate in September.

item.title: Boy, 14, stable after boat struck reef off Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq
item.description: The mother of Ben Rizzo, the 14-year-old who was left in a critical condition when a boat struck a reef off Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq on Sunday evening, said on Monday that his condition had stabilised. Yanika Rizzo shared an emotional message thanking the person who made the "lifesaving call" and urging her son to keep fighting. Ben remains in the Intensive Care Unit. A witness, Charlotte Anne Falzon, separately recounted hearing cries for help and seeing two distress flares before the vessel's lights went out and it fell silent.
